name: Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource
principle: Code acquires the same critical lock more times than intended or without a matching release on every path. Extra lock acquisitions can exhaust semaphore capacity, block forever on binary locks, or leave shared state unavailable.
detection_signals: same function calls pthread_mutex_lock(&m) twice before pthread_mutex_unlock(&m)
same function calls EnterCriticalSection(&cs) twice before LeaveCriticalSection(&cs)
same function calls sem_wait(&sem) or WaitForSingleObject(hSem, ...) multiple times before sem_post/ReleaseSemaphore
Java Lock.lock() or synchronized entry is nested on the same lock object without a matching unlock/exit
early return, break, continue, goto, or throw occurs after lock acquisition and before corresponding unlock
retry loop reacquires mutex/semaphore after failure path without releasing prior acquisition
manual lock counter or boolean guard allows lock() when alreadyHeld is true
negative_signals: pthread_mutex_lock is followed by pthread_mutex_unlock on all control-flow paths before any second lock
C++ std::lock_guard, std::unique_lock, or std::scoped_lock owns the lock in a single lexical scope
Java Lock.lock() is paired with unlock() in a finally block for every acquisition
Java synchronized block/method uses automatic monitor exit and has no nested synchronized on the same object
recursive locking uses pthread_mutexattr_settype(..., PTHREAD_MUTEX_RECURSIVE) or std::recursive_mutex and has equal unlock count
Semaphore acquire()/sem_wait() count is matched by release()/sem_post() count on all paths
false_defense_traps: checking a boolean isLocked without atomicity before lock()
using tryLock() but ignoring a false result or retrying while still holding the lock
catching exceptions after lock acquisition without unlock in finally/RAII cleanup
assuming a binary mutex is recursive without verifying mutex type
returning error after validation failure while still holding the lock
verification_focus: Can any execution path acquire the same critical resource more times than it releases before leaving, waiting, or retrying?

consequence_chains.trigger: attacker-controlled loop or request path repeatedly acquires a pooled lock/semaphore
consequence_chains.consequence: resource pool exhaustion and denial of service

consequence_chains.trigger: non-recursive binary lock is acquired again by the owning thread

patch_principle: Ensure each lock acquisition has exactly one matching unlock on every control-flow path.
Use RAII, try/finally, or scoped synchronization instead of manual unlock placement.
Release held locks before waiting, retrying, returning, or throwing, then reacquire when needed.
Avoid nested acquisition of the same non-recursive lock; refactor call paths or use a verified recursive lock only when intended.
